Data Analytics report

Segmentation checkpoint verification

Sep 9, 2026, 1:45 AM UTC

Use the packaged checkpoint for the crack prototype

The packaged `best.pt` is the stronger candidate, but full-frame drone inspection is not yet verified. On 122 test images remaining after exact train/validation-overlap exclusion, it achieved 59.6% pooled crack-mask IoU, versus 38.3% for the local one-epoch checkpoint, at confidence 0.25. Both load successfully as YOLO26s segmentation models and return masks directly from images.

Use src/ml/models/weights/segmentation/best.pt for the next prototype. Its labels are 0 = crack; 1 = pothole, but the local training, validation, and test annotations contain only class 0. Pothole quality is unverified. The larger-road-image smoke test ran without a separate detector, but showed roadside false positives and thick masks; it cannot establish drone-video quality.

The checkpoint advantage survives overlap exclusion

IoU measures overlap, not classification accuracy: true-positive crack pixels divided by the union of predicted and reference crack pixels, pooled across images. Higher is better. At confidence 0.25Source for 0.25Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels, the packaged checkpoint scores 59.6%Source for 59.6%Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels versus 38.3%Source for 38.3%Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels on the same 122Source for 122Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels images (108Source for 108Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels with reference crack pixels and 14Source for 14Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels without). Its pixel precision is 74.1%Source for 74.1%Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels and recall is 75.3%Source for 75.3%Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels; the local checkpoint reaches 68.8%Source for 68.8%Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels and 46.4%Source for 46.4%Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels, respectively.

The chart compares pooled IoU on the exact same cohort. The 21.3Source for 21.3Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels percentage-point advantage has a paired image-bootstrap 95%Source for 95%Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels percentile interval of 14.0 to 29.9Source for 29.9Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels points (2,000Source for 2,000Source: Overlap-filtered pixel metrics and paired bootstrapTable: main.clean_pixels resamples). This describes sampling uncertainty within this dataset, not transfer to drone footage.

Pool per-image pixel counts after excluding six exact training or validation matches. Paired bootstrap is recorded in robustness.json.

SELECT model, threshold, COUNT(*) AS images,
       1.0 * SUM(tp) / SUM(tp + fp + fn) AS iou,
       1.0 * SUM(tp) / SUM(tp + fp) AS precision,
       1.0 * SUM(tp) / SUM(tp + fn) AS recall
FROM clean_pixels
GROUP BY model, threshold
ORDER BY model, threshold;

Direct image inference works; drone-frame quality remains open

Both segmentation checkpoints accepted complete stored images without a preceding detector or a damage-crop step. The training recipe resizes images to 448Source for 448Source: Per-image road inference output countsFile: reports/segmentation-check/road_results.csv pixels and uses a mixed surface-image corpus; it does not document a mandatory detector-generated crop. This establishes that a separate detection stage is not required by the model interface. It does not establish that the training distribution matches wide drone road frames.

A separate smoke test used 32Source for 32Source: Per-image road inference output countsFile: reports/segmentation-check/road_results.csv seeded images from the preprocessed road-damage test directory, at inference sizes 448Source for 448Source: Per-image road inference output countsFile: reports/segmentation-check/road_results.csv and 736Source for 736Source: Per-image road inference output countsFile: reports/segmentation-check/road_results.csv, with confidence 0.25Source for 0.25Source: Per-image road inference output countsFile: reports/segmentation-check/road_results.csv. The packaged model returned masks on 11/32 and 19/32 images, respectively, with 14Source for 14Source: Per-image road inference output countsFile: reports/segmentation-check/road_results.csv and 30Source for 30Source: Per-image road inference output countsFile: reports/segmentation-check/road_results.csv instances. These are output counts, not accuracy or recall: no segmentation ground truth was evaluated for this road sample. No pothole predictions were returned. The stored images are already preprocessed; raw-frame provenance is unverified, and no video was found in the engine workspace.

Evaluation measures binary crack coverage at original resolution

  1. Load both local checkpoints with the installed Ultralytics 8.4.41 runtime and PyTorch 2.11.0. Run on CPU with four PyTorch threads; no Modal or GPU performance benchmark was performed.
  2. Infer at size 448Source for 448Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json, minimum confidence 0.10Source for 0.10Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json, with original-resolution masks (retina_masks=True). Union class-0 masks separately at thresholds 0.10Source for 0.10Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json, 0.25Source for 0.25Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json, and 0.50Source for 0.50Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json. Do not add engine enhancement, skeletonization, branch merging, or drone metadata.
  3. Read the paired grayscale reference mask and threshold it at greater than 127Source for 127Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json, matching the conversion script. Accumulate true-positive, false-positive, and false-negative pixels. Pixel precision = TP/(TP+FP); recall = TP/(TP+FN); IoU = TP/(TP+FP+FN). These pooled metrics weight images by their pixel contribution; they are not mean per-image IoU or instance mAP.
  4. Compute SHA-256Source for -256Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json hashes of images across all splits; remove sampled images identical to any training or validation image. Bootstrap the paired cleaned cohort with replacement at image level, with seed 42Source for 42Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json.
  5. Preserve selected filenames, per-image pixel counts, checkpoint metadata, road-output counts, overlays, and scripts alongside this report. Median warmed local prediction-call time was about 61 ms per 448Source for 448Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json-pixel image for either checkpoint; this includes local call overhead and is not video throughput or a GPU estimate.

The installed runtime is older than the packaged checkpoint’s embedded training version. Loading and inference succeeded, but numerical parity with the original training environment has not been established.

Split contamination and domain mismatch limit the claim

There are 58Source for 58Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json unique image hashes shared by train/test, 33 by validation/test, and 1,271 by train/validation. Six images in the 128Source for 128Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json-image sample matched training or validation; excluding them leaves 122Source for 122Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json. Exact hashing does not detect recompressed images, overlapping crops, or different frames of the same road scene. No scene-level independence claim is made.

Only 128 test images were inferred, not the entire 1,695Source for 1,695Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json-image split. The bootstrap treats sampled images as independent; scene clustering could make its interval too narrow. Zero crack predictions on the 16Source for 16Source: Evaluation results, inventory and reproducible methodFile: reports/segmentation-check/results.json original negative samples is insufficient to establish a low real-world false-positive rate, especially given the road-overlay failures.

Pothole segmentation accuracy, raw full-road-frame accuracy, drone altitude and camera transfer, temporal stability, video reading/writing, and Modal GPU throughput remain unmeasured. The road images are preprocessed still images with unverified raw-frame provenance.

Keep the simple pipeline, but separate prototype choice from release evidence

  1. Use the fingerprinted packaged checkpoint for the crack-only prototype. A Python function can pass frames directly to this segmentation model; Modal can supply GPU execution around it.
  2. Verify full-frame quality before removing detection on performance grounds. Annotate representative uncropped drone frames with road-only negatives, cracks at multiple apparent widths, and potholes. Compare direct segmentation with any proposed crop or tiling strategy on an untouched scene-disjoint evaluation set.
  3. Repair the data split and confirm class supervision before retraining. Separate by source scene, remove cross-split duplicates, audit contour-derived instance targets, and either supply pothole masks or make the model explicitly crack-only.
  4. Tune confidence on validation data, then evaluate once on held-out scenes. Report both pixel overlap and instance metrics, and check mask-width bias if downstream measurements matter.

The current engine configuration points to src/ml/models/weights/yolo26s-seg.pt, not either tested best.pt. The next implementation must select the verified checkpoint explicitly; model success in this report does not mean the existing engine already loads it.

Evidence still needed for the next decision

What are the intended drone altitude, camera angle, frame resolution, and smallest relevant crack width? Is pothole coverage required for the first version? Are there untouched raw videos and scene identifiers for a separate evaluation set? What recall and false-positive burden are acceptable? These answers determine whether full-frame resizing is sufficient or whether spatial tiling merits a measured comparison.
